about: The machine-readable agent surface for marula-core: what an agent can be granted, how it reaches it, and what it may never do. Human prose lives beside this file in README.md.

tool_derivation.rule: One tool per GET path that carries an operationId and sits under /api/, named by that operationId.
tool_derivation.capability: The first path segment after the version prefix derives the namespace, and the tool holds <namespace>:read.
tool_derivation.grant_model: Deny-by-default. filter_granted drops every namespace without a grant row, so an ungranted tool is absent from tools/list rather than refused at call time.
tool_derivation.note: Excluded prefixes and any path containing /attachments never enter the catalog, whatever the grant says.

surfaces.notes: The canonical transport, and what runs with no arguments.
The pinned API snapshot. A service key scopes what may be called.
A read of the outbox stream, not a second bus. Bounded by MARULA_EVENT_STREAM_MAXLEN.
Forward-only cursor export on (occurred_at, id). Read grant only.

sensitive.admin: Administrative surfaces. A read grant here sees configuration an ordinary technician never needs.
sensitive.migration: Migration state and control endpoints. Useful to a release tool, dangerous to an unattended agent.
sensitive.passwords: Password reset requests and state. A read here is close to an account-recovery capability.
sensitive.roles: Role definitions. Reading them is how a client learns which escalations exist.
sensitive.secrets: Secret metadata. Values stay sealed, and the metadata still maps which integration holds which key.
sensitive.settings: Instance settings, including the switches that decide what the product does under load.

prohibitions.statement: An MCP tool can never write. The catalog derives GET operations only.
A namespace without a grant row does not appear in tools/list, so the tool does not exist for that principal.
Attachments, export bundles, webhook delivery logs, API keys, auth, email, internal and portal paths never enter the catalog, whatever the grant says.
No plugin capability maps onto an administrative special, and the build fails if one ever does.
The audit trail is export only. No agent, pack or connector writes, edits or deletes a row.
A connector talks to the public API and holds no path dependency into crates/.
